summary: A brick light on a low islet in Lake Superior's Manitou passage, lit in 1867, automated in 1913, and now run by volunteers and closed to visitors.

lens.where: Great Lakes Shipwreck Museum, Whitefish Point

access.note: Grounds, dwelling and tower closed; best seen by boat (LighthouseFriends); USLHS lists it as not open to the public.

facts.agency: Gull Rock Lightkeepers and Michigan Lighthouse Conservancy

notes_for_editor: Tower height disagrees across sources: USLHS 39 ft base to lantern (record 14 m), LighthouseFriends about 45 ft, Terry Pepper 46 ft to the ventilator ball above the foundation; the story states the disagreement and the record was not changed. Light characteristic: the 2025 Light List gives Fl (2)W 5s (white); Terry Pepper and LighthouseFriends say the 1913 acetylene light was flashing red every three seconds. The record's Fl(2) W 5s is the current character; the red character is dated to 1913 only. Range: the record's 6.9 nm (ENC) and the Light List's entry were not reconciled; no range is stated in the story. Henry Corgan: the 1924 notice (Bulletin PDF p. 43) reads 'Henry Oorgan' in OCR; the index gives 1882-1885 at Gull Rock while the notice gives nine months in 1882 and continuous service after 1885; the roster has him first assistant 1885-1887. The 1866 Manitou Island service and the 1867 end date are read from OCR ('1J'til 18J7'). Nolen: the roster has him head keeper 1888-1903; Terry Pepper gives April 1897 to May 1903 from the logbook; LighthouseFriends says the family wintered in Calumet, Terry Pepper says Copper Harbor. Waldo (Nov 1913): the Calumet News headline gives a crew of 28 saved and a tug Hebard rescue in its text; LighthouseFriends describes Eagle Harbor and Portage crews with 22 men and 2 women landed at Houghton; Terry Pepper describes Copper Harbor lifesavers over four days. The story states the differences; none has been resolved. Neelon (1892) and Spokane (1912) rest on Terry Pepper alone; no primary text was found. The clippings extract (NARA RG 26 entry 13) does not print the year of the Board report it reproduces; it is cited as a clippings file. The NRHP nomination is not digitised (NPGallery PDF returns a placeholder); the listing date is from the NPGallery asset record. The 1901 retaining wall is cited to the Board's 1901 report at scan page 235; the printed page was not read. Current access: LighthouseFriends (undated) and the Gull Rock Lightkeepers site differ on emphasis; no current opening hours were found. Check before any visitor information is published. The USLHS record gives longitude -87.6597; OSM and LighthouseFriends give -87.6639 to -87.6640; the record's OSM position is kept. Fact-check 2026-10-22: Terry Pepper doubts that the fourth-order lens reportedly displayed at Whitefish Point is the station's own lens; the story states both accounts and the record's 'where' field follows LighthouseFriends, so a human should decide before the record is treated as settled. The Calumet News of 11 November 1913 (OCR) says the tug Hebard brought the captain and a crew of twenty-eight into Houghton; LighthouseFriends, quoting the 1915 Coast Guard report, gives 24 persons (22 men and two women) landed at Houghton. The story states both. The 1901 Board retaining-wall entry is on scan pages 235 and 236 (the Portland-cement coping is on 236). Henry Corgan's name is OCR'd 'Oorgan' in the 1924 notice; the index and roster spellings are used.
